before: A distributed line with a tab keeps every span at the position the tabs give it.
after: A left-to-right distributed line with a tab stretches only the text after its last tab. When that tab reaches a left stop, the text spreads from the stop to the line end; when it reaches a right, center, or decimal stop, or the text has nothing to stretch, the whole line is centered with its tab positions.
reason: Only layout geometry changes. Canonical OOXML, source positions, operations, and collaboration formats remain unchanged. Tab spans carry the alignment of the stop they reached as a derived layout field. Every peer derives the same geometry from the same document parts.
